themes.theme: primitive or low-poly model where a kit model belongs
themes.what: Read by sentence, the kit person (no. 42 rounds 1 to 4, after the 2026-10-03 fix) and the kit semi_truck (no. 41, all three judges, rounds 1 to 5). The person could not change under no. 43, which was mid-panel and calls it on three frames, so it is deferred to the next pass with a note in ILLUSTRATION_SYSTEM.md. The tractor was fixed in assets/js/kit/vehicles.js at the judges' named fix: two-piece windscreen in a coated glass with wipers and a visor, a grille surround over a recessed core with vertical bars, twin lamps in chrome bezels, an arch flare, a cowl seam and louvres. Proven before and after through examples/kit/build.py's page() and the carousel engine, sizes.py 110 of 110.

The kit school_bus's yellow lip across the front wheel (queue school-bus-hood-lip-across-front-wheel, no. 42) was a self-overlapping lobe in the body's profile and is gone. The rest of the theme is the engine's or a chassis's near plane (queue near-plane-zfight-on-card-skins), written up in UPGRADE_BACKLOG 2026-10-05 item 8.

themes.theme: acceptance lists a frame missing its subject would pass (queue acceptance-lists-trivially-satisfiable)
themes.what: Queue repeat 2 (nos. 41, 42, 43), which made this pass due. scripts/carousel/dossier_check.py fails a storyboard dated from 2026-10-06 whose frame's acceptance list never names its CRAFT PLAN largest object or sets no floor on a visible size of the art. Replayed: 44 of 45 frames across nos. 38, 40, 41, 42 and 43 had no floor. The digest's word themes do not count this one, so its rounds are not counted.

themes.theme: no contact, dirt or grime where things meet the ground
themes.what: The engine's (human). Named on no. 41 and no. 42 after the 2026-10-03 maintainer fix, so the fix did not hold at the panel's eye. UPGRADE_BACKLOG 2026-10-05 item 8.

themes.theme: largest object unmodelled (slab, bare wall, clean clay)
themes.what: The acceptance floor now makes each frame's list name the CRAFT PLAN largest object, so a critic grading the list checks the object the plan promised to model. The objects themselves differ per deck.
